alignments.note: Article rendered by the demonstrative standing where the phrase's the would stand (rule 41).
Italic supplied clause with its subject; no morpheme in the verse licenses either word, and the two stand together doing one office (rules 2, 7, 17, 20).
The passive recasting states nothing of this preposition's own relation; the margin's by his hand upon me is set aside for the printed text (rules 38, 40).

The suffix of עָלַי takes the English pronoun that realizes it. Rule 40 places such a suffix where the recasting silences its preposition, including a subject pronoun, as in וְקֹרָא לָךְ → and thou shalt be called: the ASV's passive makes the person this suffix denotes the English subject. Rule 17's permission reaches a pronoun realizing the verb's own person and number, and this I does not realize the 3ms הִשְׂכִּיל.

Hiphil recast as an English passive with its auxiliaries, headed on the lexical verb of the complement (rules 24, 44); the unit is discontinuous around the subject pronoun, which answers to the suffix of עָלַי rather than to this verb (rule 25).
Appositional even with no marker and no connective morpheme in the clause to license it (rules 14, 16).
Article on the rectum rendered by the demonstrative standing where its the would stand (rule 41).
Rectum with its of, discontinuous around the demonstrative (rules 19, 25).

review_notes: Corrected: the English subject I was assigned to הִשְׂכִּיל and the suffix of עָלַי left unrepresented. The Hebrew verb is 3ms and the ASV's passive drops its agent, so I realizes no person of that verb; it realizes the suffix, which rule 40 places precisely in this recasting, and rule 2 forbids leaving a written morpheme unrepresented while an English word plainly realizing it stands assigned elsewhere. עַל itself remains unrepresented, its relation unstated.
The marginal alternative (Jehovah made me understand in writing by his hand upon me) was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
said David is one added run of italic supply and even a second added unit; the ASV's own rendered material stands between them (rules 2, 7).
